questions.question: A change in the constitution made by the supreme legislative body in a country is known as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e., **__Constitutional Amendment__**

 
• **The Constitutional Amendment** is the formal change in the text of the written Constitution of a nation or state.
 
• **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution gives for the procedure of the Constitutional Amendments.
 
• Some of the** important provisions** of the Constitutional Amendment of India are :
 
 
• It can be laid in any house of the Indian Parliament.
 
• The bill can be introduced either by a minister or a private member.
 
• It cannot be introduced in the state legislature.
 
• The bill must be passed by each house separately.
 
• It should be passed by a special majority (2/3rd of the members present and voting and not less than 50% of the strength).
 
• The ratification of at least half of the states is required in case of amendment of any federal feature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Once the **President** gives his **assent**, the Bill will become an **Act.**
 
 
 
• **​**There has been** 104 amendments** of the Constitution of India as of March 2020.

__
 
• **Articles 1 - 4** of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory.
 
• These articles define the name and territory of the Union, admission or establishment of new states, formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• Article 1 declares India as a Union of States, emphasizing its indestructible nature.
 
• Article 2 empowers the Parliament to admit or establish new states into the Union.
 
• Article 3 provides the procedure for the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• Article 4 specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for the admission/establishment of new states or alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states are not to be considered amendments of the Constitution under Article 368.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 1, the territory of India can be classified into three categories:

 
 
• Territories of the states
 
• Union territories
 
• Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time. 
 
 
 
• Article 1 of the Indian constitution:
 
 
• India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
 
 
 
• The names of states and union territories and their territorial extent are mentioned in the first schedule of the Constitution.
 
• The first Schedule contains:
 
 
• Names of the States and their territorial jurisdiction.
 
• Names of the Union Territories and their extent.
 
 
 
• Notably, the ‘Territory of India’ is a wider expression than the ‘Union of India’ because the latter includes only states while the former includes not only the states but also union territories and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any future time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Article 2 of the Indian Constitution** deals with the admission or** establishment of new states in the Union of India**.

 
 
• It provides for the power of the** Parliament to admit new states, or to establish new states by separating territory from any existing state or by merging two or more states or parts of states.**
 
 
 
• **Article 10** of the Constitution deals with the power of the Parliament to make laws with respect to the **reorganization of states**.
 
 
• It provides that Parliament may by** law admit new states into the Union, or establish new states by separating territory from any existing state or by merging two or more states or parts of states.**
 
 
 
• ** Article 11** of the Constitution provides for the power of the President to make certain modifications to the boundaries of states,** subject to certain conditions and procedures.**
 
 
• It states that the** President may by order, after consultation with the Governor of the state concerned, make certain changes to the boundaries of any state or alter the name, area or boundaries of any Union territory.**

• The Constitution of India does not provide for dual citizenship.
 
• India follows a single citizenship policy, which means that a person is a citizen of India only and not of any state individually.
 
• Dual citizenship could lead to complications in matters of loyalty and allegiance, thus the Indian Constitution avoids it.
 
• Other countries may allow dual citizenship, but India mandates renouncing Indian citizenship upon acquiring foreign nationality.

• It ensures equality and inclusiveness in the electoral process.
 
• Every citizen above the age of 18 has the right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assemblies.

• It refers to a judiciary that is free from any influence or control by the executive or the legislature.
 
• The Indian Constitution ensures the independence of the judiciary through various provisions such as the security of tenure, fixed service conditions, and restrictions on practice after retirement.
 
• Judicial independence is crucial for the fair administration of justice and upholding the rule of law.

• The Indian Constitution is a unique blend of rigidity and flexibility.
 
• Some parts of the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority, while others require a special majority or ratification by half of the state legislatures.
 
• This blend allows the Constitution to adapt to changing needs while preserving its core principles.
 
• Article 368 of the Constitution provides for the amendment process.

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens?

__
 
• **Five types of writs** can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens.
 
• These writs are: **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto,** and **Certiorari**.
 
• The power to issue these writs is granted to the Supreme Court under **Article 32** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is issued to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and to set them free if such detention is found illegal.
 
• The writ of **Mandamus** commands a public authority to perform a public duty.
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• The writ of **Quo-Warranto** is issued to prevent a person from holding a public office to which they are not entitled.
 
• The writ of **Certiorari** is issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court for review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs not only for Fundamental Rights but also for other purposes under **Article 139** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the High Courts have the power to issue writs under **Article 226** of the Constitution.
 
• The writ jurisdiction of the High Courts is broader as it is not confined to the protection of Fundamental Rights alone.

• The Concurrent List allows both the Union and the State Governments to legislate on certain matters.
 
• This list includes subjects like marriage, bankruptcy, trade unions, and education.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a concurrent subject, the law made by the Union Government prevails.
 
• The inclusion of the Concurrent List ensures a balance of power and responsibilities between the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It includes matters of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• There are 97 subjects listed under the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

• The State List comprises subjects on which only the state governments can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of local or state importance such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• There are 66 subjects listed under the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• It contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• This schedule is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Residual powers refer to subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, residual powers rest with the Union Government.
 
• This provision ensures that any new subject of legislation that arises is dealt with at the national level.

questions.question: The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a _________ system of government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary system**

 
 
• The **Constitution of India** is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a **parliamentary system of government**.
 
• **India **has a parliamentary system of **government **with federal and unitary components.
 
• It is a sovereign** socialist, secular, **and **democratic** **republic**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the head of the **Council of Ministers**, which provides advice to the **President**, who is the nation's constitutional leader.
 
• The** Indian Constitution**, which was approved by the Constituent Assembly on** November 26, 1949**, and took effect on **January 26, 1950**, governs the **Country**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​**The **head **of state in a **parliamentary system **is often a different person from the head of **government**. In contrast, in a presidential system, the executive branch does not receive its democratic legitimacy from the legislative and the head of state frequently doubles as the head of **government**.
 
• A **parliamentary** **system**, sometimes known as a parliamentarian democracy, is a form of democratic government in which the executive branch obtains the backing of the legislative, usually a **parliament**, to whom it is answerable.

questions.question: ​As per the Constitution of India, every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of ________ hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**twenty-four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An arrested person should be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest.**
 
• **Article 22 **of the Indian constitution provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• These 24 hours are** excluded from the time necessary for the journey** from the place of arrest to the court of the Magistrate.
 
• No such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a Magistrate.
 
• **Preventive detention** refers to taking one who has not committed a crime into custody by considering him as a threat to law and order.
 
• A person may be taken to preventive custody only for 3 months at the first instance.
 
• **Article 22(2):**
 
 
• **Clause (2)** of Article 22 states that- "Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of 24 hours".
 
• Such arrest excludes the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate.
 
• No such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 22(4):**

 
 
• **Clause (4) **of the Article states- "that no individual can be detained for more than 3 months."
 
• Unless a bench of High court judges or an Advisory board decides to extend the date.
 
 
 
• **Article 22(5):**
 
 
• **Clause (5) **of Article 22 states- "that the detained individual should be made aware of the grounds he/she has been detained."
 
• And should provide him/her with an opportunity of making a representation against the case.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between preventive detention and an arrest:**

 
 
• An 'arrest' is done when a person is charged with a crime. An arrested person is produced before a magistrate within the next 24 hours.
 
• In the case of 'preventive detention, a person is detained as he/she is simply restricted from doing something that might deteriorate the law and order situation.
 
 
 
• **The preventive detention laws** made by the Parliament are:
 
 
• Preventive Detention Act, 1950. Expired in 1969.
 
• Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), 1971. Repealed in 1978.
 
• Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act (COFEPOSA), 1974.
 
• National Security Act (NSA), 1980.
 
• Prevention of Black Marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act (PBMSECA), 1980.
 
• Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act (TADA), 1985. Repealed in 1995.
 
• Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (PITNDPSA), 1988.
 
• Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA), 2002. Repealed in 2004.

questions.question: The term ‘secular’ was added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'secular' was added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in the year **1976**.
 
• This amendment is also known as the **Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976**.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is one of the most comprehensive amendments made to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The amendment emphasized the **democratic and secular fabric** of the Indian state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism**

 
 
• Secularism in the Indian context means that the state shall not discriminate against any citizen on the basis of religion and treats all religions with equal respect.
 
• It ensures that individuals have the freedom to practice, profess, and propagate any religion of their choice.
 
• In India, it also means the separation of religion from political, economic, social, and cultural spheres of life.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• This amendment is known for its **extensive changes** to the Constitution, often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging modifications.
 
• Besides adding the term "secular", it also added the term "socialist" to the Preamble.
 
• It laid down Fundamental Duties of citizens under Part IV-A (Article 51A).
 
• It attempted to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the Parliament and the executive.
 
 
 
• **Preamble of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• The Preamble is an introductory statement that sets out the guiding purposes and principles of the Constitution.
 
• It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.
 
• The Preamble outlines the objectives of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Although it is not enforceable by law, it is a crucial guide to the interpretation of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Habeas corpus**__.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **special order of the courts, Habeas corpus**, means **“arrested person should be presented before the court"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a legal remedy that **allows a person to inform a court about an illegitimate arrest or imprisonment** and ask that the court compel the person's custodian—typically a prison official—to bring the prisoner to court so that the validity of the arrest can be determined.
 
• **William Blackstone **referred to the **writ of habeas corpus** as a** "great and efficient writ in all manner of illrgal confinement"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a summons that has the** same legal effect as a court order**; it is** directed to the custodian and requests that a prisoner be brought before the court together with documentation of the custodian's authority** so that the court can evaluate if the custodian has the right to hold the prisoner

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• .A **judicial remedy **known as a **mandamus** is an** order from a court to any government, subordinate court, corporation, or public authority** directing them to perform (or refrain from performing) a particular act that they are legally required to perform (or refrain from performing), and which is in the nature of a public duty and, in some cases, a **statutory duty**.
 
• **Certiorari** is a legal procedure **used to ask for judicial review of a ruling made by a lower court or government** **body**.
 
• A writ of prerogative known as a **quo warranto demands that the person to whom it is addressed provide proof of their legal capacity** to exercise a right, power, or franchise.
